target.title: fix(config): stop repeated legacy config-health warnings
target.body:
Closes #99280.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway restart`, and `openclaw doctor` could keep warning that `logs/config-health.json` conflicted with shared SQLite state even when the legacy JSON described the same config baseline already stored in SQLite.

## Why This Change Was Made

The legacy config-health migration now compares existing SQLite rows against legacy JSON by stable config fingerprint fields instead of raw JSON string equality. It normalizes file mode to permission bits and ignores volatile fingerprint fields such as observation and stat timestamps, while still leaving the legacy source in place when the config hash or suspicious signature truly differs.

## User Impact

Users with already-migrated config-health state no longer get a permanent, unresolvable legacy migration warning on every status, restart, or doctor command. Real conflicts are still preserved for operator review instead of being archived silently.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — passed, 40 tests including new coverage for matching config-health fingerprints with timestamp/mode drift and for real hash conflicts.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/state-migrations.ts src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts` — passed.
- `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.ts src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.non-agents.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-non-agents.issue-99280.tsbuildinfo` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
